title: Rectification Periods for Faults, Recalls and Safety Defects
content:
Where a fault stands on a vehicle in a Keyturn Vehicle Listing class, three periods decide how long the host has: one for an ordinary fault, one for an open safety recall, and one measured in hours for a safety defect.

| Class | Ordinary fault rectification (calendar days) | Open safety recall rectification (calendar days) | Safety defect grace (hours) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Keyturn Economy Class Listing | 14 | 30 | 24 |
| Keyturn Standard Class Listing | 14 | 30 | 24 |
| Keyturn Premium Class Listing | 10 | 21 | 12 |
| Keyturn Luxury Class Listing | 7 | 14 | 12 |
| Keyturn Exotic Class Listing | 5 | 10 | 6 |
| Keyturn Commercial Van Class Listing | 7 | 21 | 12 |

The first two columns are counted in whole calendar days; the third is counted in whole elapsed hours. In every class the recall period is the longer of the two day periods, and the safety defect grace never exceeds 24 hours in any class and falls to 6 hours in the Keyturn Exotic Class Listing.
